description_short.value: Accra-based universal bank, founded in 1994 as a merchant bank, serving corporate, business and personal customers; listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange in December 2025.
description_short.source: Written by us from the First Atlantic Bank PLC 2025 Annual Report (corporate profile; report of the directors, principal activities) and the IPO prospectus (section 3.1, corporate history)

description_full.value: First Atlantic Bank PLC is a Ghanaian universal bank licensed under the Banks and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Act, 2016. It does corporate, investment and retail banking, organised as Corporate Banking, Personal and Business Banking, and Prestige Banking, with dedicated public-sector and digital units. At the time of its IPO it had 35 branches. The bank was incorporated on 4 May 1994 as First Atlantic Merchant Bank Limited and began business on 28 August 1995 under a Bank of Ghana licence. It became First Atlantic Bank Limited in 2010 and converted to a public company, First Atlantic Bank PLC, on 7 November 2025. It owns 55% of First Atlantic Brokers, a Ghana Stock Exchange dealer, and has a significant stake in First Atlantic Asset Management. In December 2025 it offered 101.7 million shares at GHS 7.30 in an IPO: about 22.6 million new shares, with the rest sold by existing shareholders. It then listed all its shares on the Ghana Stock Exchange, with trading starting on 19 December 2025. At the end of 2025 Kedari Nominees held 46.6% of the shares and AFIG Fund II 21.0%, followed by Ghanaian pension schemes. Its registered office is Atlantic Place, No. 1 Seventh Avenue, Ridge West, Accra. It reports in Ghana cedis, with a financial year ending 31 December.
